description: Self-hosted version of Microsoft's OmniParser Image-to-text model

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted FastAPI server that wraps Microsoft's OmniParser model to convert UI screenshots into structured element lists with bounding boxes.
summary.what_it_does: The repository packages Microsoft's OmniParser image-to-text model as a self-hosted service. Its Dockerfile starts from the Hugging Face demo image to get model weights and utility functions, then adds a FastAPI server in main.py to serve the model directly. The API has a single route, /process_image, which takes a UI screenshot. It returns three things: the image with bounding boxes drawn on it (base64-encoded), a list of parsed elements with text descriptions, and the bounding box coordinates of each element. The README says the author chose direct serving over Gradio because it is faster and avoids Hugging Face rate limits. The README also points to fly.toml for Fly.io deployment.
use_cases: parse UI screenshots into structured elements for an LLM agent
detect clickable icons and buttons in a screenshot
get bounding box coordinates of UI elements
host an OmniParser endpoint on my own server
deploy a screen parsing API to fly.io
avoid Hugging Face Gradio rate limits for screen parsing
how_to_run: Build the docker image: docker build -t omni-parser-app .
Run the docker container: docker run -p 7860:7860 omni-parser-app
Optionally deploy to fly.io by running: fly launch and following the prompts
stack: OmniParser (Microsoft model, weights from Hugging Face demo image)
notable: Serves the OmniParser model directly through FastAPI instead of Gradio, which the author says is faster
Single /process_image route returns annotated image, parsed elements, and bounding boxes
Includes fly.toml and README instructions for one-command Fly.io deployment
Builds on the Hugging Face demo image to reuse its weights and utility functions
caveats: Requires a GPU and about 16 GB of RAM (swap recommended), per the README
The README's API docs link is truncated, so the docs location is not clear
Related-projects section mentions OneQuery, but the README gives no other usage details
